featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coffee Purist’s Haven in a Serene Locale.

Blue Tokai in Breach Candy is less of a typical café and more of a sanctuary for serious coffee lovers. Located on a quiet, leafy lane, it provides an escape from the city’s hustle without compromising on a world-class caffeine fix.

The Coffee & Food (4.5/5):
The coffee is, of course, the hero. I ordered a pour-over of their seasonal roast (a Kenyan) and a flat white. Both were brewed to perfection – balanced, aromatic, and showcasing the beans’ distinct notes. The baristas are knowledgeable and happy to explain the profiles. The food menu is thoughtfully curated to complement the coffee. The Avocado & Feta Toast on sourdough was fresh and satisfying, and the Almond Croissant was flaky and buttery. It’s simple, quality fare that doesn't distract from the main event.

Ambiance & Service (4/5):
The space is modern, minimalist, and flooded with natural light. The high ceilings, clean lines, and wooden accents create a calm, focused atmosphere. It’s ideal for reading, working solo, or having a quiet conversation. Service is efficient and polite, though it can feel a bit reserved – the staff are more artisans than greeters, which fits the vibe.

Considerations:

It’s a destination for coffee. If you’re looking for a full, loud brunch scene or sugary flavored lattes, this isn’t it.

Seating can be limited during peak weekend mornings, especially the coveted window spots.

Parking in Breach Candy can be a challenge; consider using a ride-share.

Verdict:
Blue Tokai Breach Candy is a gem for anyone who appreciates specialty coffee in a serene, stylish setting. It’s a place to slow down, savor your cup, and enjoy a moment of quiet productivity or reflection. You come for the exceptional coffee, and you stay for the peaceful ambiance. A definite recommend for a quality caffeine retreat.

This place was on our list of must visit South Indian restaurants.

We ordered,

2. Ghee Podi Idli - Good
3. Garlic Mulbagal Dosa - Good (Most places in Mumbai that promise a Benne end up giving you a Mulbagal-esque dish although the ingredients are not all the same)

Good luck!

featured_reviews.name: Amrutjyoti Shinde
featured_reviews.review_text: Heard a lot about this place from reels, and was not disappointed. Went with 3 friends around 3:30 pm on 14th Feb. It was not crowded at all. Started with the Iced Filter Coffee, was a little watered down, but you can always ask for more coffee concoction. Then the Goli Bhaji and Mangalore Buns were absolutely delicious, not too sweet, perfectly balancing the sweetness with the coconut chutney. Then we got 4 different doses, and the Ghee Podi Benne Masala Dosa (jain) was the bestseller for a reason. First bite was heavenly and comforting, and the masala was made of raw banana, and was in sufficient quantity. The dosa was only so flavorful, there was no need of sambar or chutney. If you take regular dosa, you get an additional tomato garlic chutney. My friend ordered the Mulbagal Dosa, which they claim to have started the 1st time in Mumbai. Some might say you would get doses at cheaper prices elsewhere, but their price reflects their commitment to perfection and love towards serving people. I will definitely visit this place again..!!

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
An unforgettable Thai brunch experience that truly transported us straight to the bustling streets of Bangkok 🇹🇭✨
We recently attended the Tuk Tuk Tales pop-up at Plate & Pint curated by the incredibly talented Chef Akanksha Saigal, and every single dish on the menu reflected her passion, creativity, and deep understanding of authentic Thai flavours.
We went as a group of friends for brunch, and honestly, it turned into one of those meals where every plate sparks conversation, every bite feels memorable, and time just flies by over great food and even better company. The vibe at Plate & Pint added so much warmth to the experience — lively, cozy, vibrant, and perfect for a long indulgent afternoon.
The meal began with the Mango & Avocado Ceviche — incredibly fresh, bright, and beautifully balanced with chilli, lime, cilantro, green apple, and crispy shallots adding layers of texture and zing. A refreshing start that instantly awakened the palate.
The Crispy Potato Stacks were an absolute standout. Perfectly crisp with rich green curry notes, aromatic fried basil, chilli crackling, and toasted herb rice bringing together comfort and complexity in every bite.
The Gai Yang Thai BBQ Chicken was beautifully charred and deeply flavourful, paired wonderfully with pickled cucumber, pickled chilli, and a delicious dipping sauce that elevated the smokiness of the chicken.
The Spicy Tamarind Glaze dishes were another highlight. Both the cottage cheese and pork belly versions were packed with bold sweet spicy flavours and had that addictive Thai style balance that keeps you reaching for another bite.
For mains, the Holy Basil Stir Fry was pure comfort food done right. Fragrant basil, juicy chicken, cucumber, fluffy rice, and a fried egg made this dish hearty, satisfying, and incredibly soulful.
The Tom Yum Hot Pot was bursting with authentic Thai aromatics — lemongrass, galangal, lime leaf — with the prawns soaking beautifully in the deeply comforting broth. Warm, sharp, spicy, and layered with flavour.
And of course, no Thai meal feels complete without a great Pad Thai, and this one absolutely delivered. Perfectly cooked rice noodles coated in tamarind sauce with chicken, bean sprouts, and peanuts creating the ideal balance of sweet, savoury, nutty, and tangy flavours.
Dessert was the perfect finale — Mango Sticky Rice with tender coconut ice cream. Rich, fragrant, comforting, and tropical all at once. Easily one of the best versions we’ve had in Mumbai.
The cocktails were equally thoughtful and fun, especially the Thai Chilli Guava Michelada and Mango Chilli White Wine Spritz, which paired beautifully with the food and added another vibrant layer to the entire experience.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If South Mumbai’s cafe culture had to be summed up in one place, this would be it. Cafe Free India brings together great food, a lively setting, and an atmosphere that keeps you hooked from the moment you walk in.

The space carries a strong Goan inspired vibe, paired with an energy that feels vibrant and effortless. What truly sets it apart is the 📍Live Karaoke hosted Four Times a week ( Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, 9pm onwards ) It adds a sense of excitement to the entire experience and makes the place feel dynamic and interactive.

The food here leans towards indulgent comfort. The parmesan corn ribs are juicy and full of flavour, while the honey chilli lotus root stands out with the perfect balance of sweet and spice. Their pizzas are rich, cheesy, and consistently satisfying.

The drinks menu keeps things interesting with beers on tap and cocktails inspired by iconic parts of Mumbai like the Sea Link. Seasonal additions like the mango chilli margarita bring in a refreshing twist.

When it comes to desserts, this is where you should absolutely give in. The gooey brownie with vanilla ice cream paired with an irresistible mango cream is easily one of the highlights and something you cannot go wrong with.

Overall, Cafe Free India in Lower Parel delivers more than just a meal. With its food, drinks, and high energy karaoke nights, it is a place that promises a fun and memorable outing.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The ambiance is one of the highlights, with a comfortable setting and friendly service, making it a nice place to spend time.

featured_reviews.review_text: We recently visited this newly opened cafe @iteeha.coffee store in Mahalaxmi. This place has an amazing soothing ambience and I’m totally in love with it. Not only the ambience is comforting but the food is so good that you’ll be wanting more. We tried their Mac & Cheese which was exactly perfect for the quote don’t judge a book by its cover😂 It looked a little sad but honestly it’s one of the best mac & cheese I’ve ever tasted. The second was the Ham and Cheese sandwich, this is the dish that stuck in my mind. It’s super yummy and even after a few days of visit I’m still craving for more. The next was Butter croissant, it was flaky, crispy and loaded with butter. Chicken Quiche was our next choice. The pastry was perfectly golden and crispy and it’s definitely a good one. For beverages, we tried their House cold coffee with Vanilla bean ice cream, it’s definitely a must try for all those who love thick coffee shake. We even tried their Mocha which was also amazing. • Veg Quiche:- Quiche is basically a custard baked in a flaky pie crust shell. It's stuffed with various options and is enjoyed by every one. Here we tried is the veg quiche which had cheese and leek.
• Chicken Quiche :- Similar to the up one, only difference is it has chicken stuffing.
• Ham & Cheese Sandwich:- This one absolutely had my heart. Super super delicious crisp sandwich. The classic sandwich which never fails to amaze you.
• Classic Chicken Sandwich :- Great great filling absolutely different than we usually get and would anyday go for this one. Chicken lovers, this crisp amazing delicious Sandwich is worth a try.
• Chocolate Cake :- One of the best chocolate cakes I have had. Soft, melting in mouth this cake has my heart.

featured_reviews.name: D M
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I were to rate the cafe's concept, it would be a 5! But if you ask me about my overall experience, it will be strictly a 3.

The ambience is bang on perfect for hanging out with friends. There are books stacked like a mini library which you can read while you enjoy a bite. The food that we tried was so not great though. We tried:

•White sauce chicken pasta
•Chicken B2BLC sandwich
•Cold coffee with almond milk (of which the almond milk quantity was only available for 1 serve. Disappointing.)
•Cold coffee with hazelnut
•Paneer pesto crepe
•Chicken fingers

Overall, the pasta was the winner. It was cooked very well with the sauce tasting creamy and delicious. It was served with the normal bread cut into triangles and toasted. The sandwich size was quite huge with a good amount of filling. Not at all a fan of both the cold coffees - One with almond milk and the other with cow milk. The paneer pesto wrap didn’t have salt and the taste was quite off and not balanced. It’s supposed to be creamy but instead we could taste only the greens. It was a total letdown. The crepe covering was nice though but again what’s the point? Chicken fingers seemed a bit over-fried and stale served with a sauce (it was definitely not mayonnaise as told to us) which did not go well. We chose not to eat all 6 pieces as a result.

The service was alright. The server made a face when we could not finish everything on the plate and commented that it would be given to someone else. Now I understand that’s very noble of them to do that to prevent food wastage. I politely replied on the same lines with a smile. His tone seemed rude nor were there any other mannerisms leaving us baffled and uncomfortable.

Overall not a great experience and would skip returning.

featured_reviews.name: Prajakta Chorge
featured_reviews.review_text: The staff members are very welcoming. I enjoyed the cafe bonbon; it is quite good if you appreciate a strong coffee. I truly love both the place and its ambiance. I would highly recommend it for meeting with friends and it's also a wonderful spot for book lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay to Barcelona is a must-visit café if you’re in Mumbai!
The food here is amazing and the vibe is just perfect. Absolutely loved the paneer pesto sandwich and the coffees are really good too .

featured_reviews.name: Avi Kadu
featured_reviews.review_text:
First of all, gratitude to the owner for working towards the development of the society. I have also read your personal journey, and it is truly inspiring to see where you started and what you have built today.
However, I would like to share my honest feedback about the food quality and service, which was disappointing during our visit.
I ordered a coffee, but it was not hot. I finished it quietly without creating any issue; you may even check the CCTV if required. However, proper serving temperature should be ensured.
We ordered a chicken omelette with cheese, but honestly, it was difficult to find the chicken in it. Initially, I thought there might be chunks inside, but there were no visible shreds or proper quantity. That was quite disappointing.
We also ordered nachni pancakes, and the dish was served with cold caramel sauce that seemed straight from the fridge.
Ideally, the server should inform whether the sauce will be served on the side or on top. Warm pancakes with apple and caramel sauce should not be cold, as it completely spoils the taste of the dish.
When the bill came, the lady at the counter suggested we need not pay due to the experience. However, we respect your effort and the noble work you are doing, so we chose to pay.
Sir, basic training for the chef and kitchen team is necessary. My child is autistic, and after waiting patiently for quite some time, receiving such food was disappointing for us. Eventually, we left the place dissatisfied.
I must mention that the server was good and well-trained, but he was slightly pushy while promoting initiatives. Sometimes this can irritate guests, so a balanced approach would help.
Please understand that we are genuine food lovers and not here to damage anyone’s reputation. We appreciate your noble work and truly hope you continue doing it. Just focus a little more on food quality, serving standards, and taste, and the place can become even better.
✅ Suggested Next Step:
If you want, I can also create a shorter, sharper Google review (more impactful and slightly aggressive) which usually gets faster attention from restaurant management.

featured_reviews.name: Stephen Antu Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! The ambience is calm, welcoming, and has a beautiful vibe that instantly makes you feel at ease. I tried the Pink Sauce Pasta and the Spanish Omelette—the food was really good and well-prepared.

The service was handled by Jyoti (I hope I’ve got the name right—referring to the tall girl who also models), and she was excellent throughout. There was a small glitch in service because of which we couldn’t fully enjoy the Spanish Omelette, but Kushboo handled the feedback very gracefully. The way she spoke about the café’s story and its origin was truly inspiring.

It’s not just a café—it’s a place with a heart. Definitely worth visiting, especially to hear the story from Kushboo herself.

I’m giving one star less only because there’s room for improvement in the service, which I’m sure can be fixed with a little bit of training.
